title: Scalar Quantity
content: A scalar quantity is a physical quantity that has only magnitude and is completely described by a single number with an appropriate unit.
e: A scalar quantity is a physical quantity that has only magnitude and is completely described by a single number with an appropriate unit. Scalar Quantity is a quantity that has magnitude only. A scalar is done once you have the size and the unit.

title: Vector Quantity
content: A vector quantity is a physical quantity that has both magnitude and a directional quality.
e: A vector quantity is a physical quantity that has both magnitude and a directional quality. Vector Quantity is a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

title: Distance
content: Distance (or distance travelled by the body) is the length of the path along which the body moves.
e: Distance (or distance travelled by the body) is the length of the path along which the body moves. Distance is the path length travelled, with no direction. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start.

title: Displacement
content: Displacement is the distance travelled along a particular direction, directed from the starting point to the end point.
e: Displacement is the distance travelled along a particular direction, directed from the starting point to the end point. Displacement is the straight directed change from start point to end point. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start.

title: Average Speed
content: The average speed is the ratio of total distance to time taken.
e: The average speed is the ratio of total distance to time taken. Average Speed is how fast the path length changes, with no direction.

title: Average Velocity
content: The average velocity is the ratio of total displacement to time taken.
e: The average velocity is the ratio of total displacement to time taken. Average Velocity is displacement per time, so direction matters. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

title: Instantaneous Speed
content: Instantaneous speed is defined as the time rate of change of distance.
e: Instantaneous speed is defined as the time rate of change of distance. Instantaneous Speed is how fast the path length changes, with no direction. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

title: Instantaneous Velocity
content: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of displacement.
e: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of displacement. Instantaneous Velocity is displacement per time, so direction matters. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

title: Instantaneous Acceleration
content: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity.
e: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity. Instantaneous Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.
